senses.definition: To write something down where it will outlive whatever made it: a process restart, a page refresh, the end of a session. The noun for this concern is persistence, and the persistence layer is wherever that durable copy is kept.
senses.caution: Engineers hear a specific promise in it, that the thing is on durable storage and will come back after a crash, so do not use it for a value you are holding in a variable or a cache. It is transitive here, and that is the tell: you persist the state. Ordinary English uses the same word intransitively for keeping at something, so the team persisted says nothing at all about data, and we persisted the results will simply not parse for anyone non-technical in the room.
senses.example: Right now the session only lives in memory. If the pod restarts we lose the whole conversation, so we need to persist it.

cues.text: A prototype loses everything the user typed the moment the browser is refreshed, and you are writing the ticket for what has to change.
In a design review someone is holding session state in memory on a single node, and you want to name the missing property before it goes near production.
An architect asks where the agent's conversation history lives after a pod restarts, and you want the verb for putting it somewhere that survives one.

distractors: To hold a connection open between requests so that the next one does not pay again for setting it up.
To keep a copy close to whoever is asking so that repeat reads come back fast, on the understanding that the copy is disposable and can be rebuilt from source whenever it is wrong.

To take a copy to a second location on a schedule so that there is something to restore from if the first one is lost. Nobody reads from that copy while things are going well, which is why it is so often found broken.

To flatten a structure into a run of bytes so that it can cross a network and be rebuilt into the same shape at the other end. The concern is the format on the wire, and both sides have to agree on it before anything useful moves.

To keep two systems in agreement as records change on either side, applying an agreed rule to decide which version wins when both of them moved at the same moment. Almost all of the work is in the reconciliation rather than in the writing, and almost all of the bugs are there too.

senses.definition: Staying with something well past the point where most people stop. It names the trait rather than the result, and always implies something was pushing back.
senses.caution: Praise for persistence quietly says the person got there by not stopping, which makes it a consolation prize when the work actually succeeded on merit: told to someone whose analysis was simply the best in the room, it damns them. Persistent about a person is worse again, because in most rooms that is the word for someone who will not take no for an answer.
senses.example: That deal closed on persistence more than anything else. She went back to them four times after we had all written it off.

cues.text: A friend got into medical school on their third application, and you are raising a glass to whatever it was that got them there.
Your son has been failing the same climbing route every Saturday for a month, and today he got up it.
You are writing a reference for someone whose strongest quality is that they never let a thing drop.
A neighbour finally got the council to replace the broken streetlight after a year of letters nobody answered.

distractors: The ability to come back quickly after a setback, more or less as you were before it.
A willingness to take on the work nobody else wants, usually because it is dull rather than because it is difficult.
Refusing to move from a position even once the evidence against it has been laid out, which reads as conviction from the inside and as obstinacy from anywhere else.
Care and attention to detail held at the same level over long stretches of work, so that the last page gets exactly the treatment the first one did, long after anybody would notice if it had not.

Confidence that a plan will come good in spite of what the people around you think, held firmly enough that you carry on funding it out of your own budget. It is a judgement about the odds, and it is either vindicated in the end or it is not.
